profile.reading: This is Orange Polskas Warsaw Data Hub at Aleja Krakowska 180 in Lazy, in the Warsaw metropolitan area, opened in October 2021 following roughly 14 months of construction by Polish general contractor Warbud. The building totals about 6,700 square meters, or roughly 72,000 square feet, housing four data halls of 400 square meters each, together about 1,600 square meters, or roughly 17,200 square feet, of technical whitespace. The facility was built with N plus 1 precision air conditioning, independent chilled water cooling loops, gas based fire suppression, early smoke detection, and laser and biometric security systems, and Orange has described it as one of the most innovative facilities of its type in Poland, hosting both the companys own network infrastructure and third party colocation and hosting customers. Power capacity in megawatts was not disclosed in sourcing found this session. Orange Polska traces its roots to Telekomunikacja Polska, spun out of Polands state postal and telecommunications administration on December 4, 1991 and beginning operations January 1, 1992. The company listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange in 2000, the same year France Telecom and Polish investment group Kulczyk Holding acquired a 35 percent stake, which France Telecom expanded in 2001, building majority control by 2002 and completing full privatization in May 2010. The company was renamed Orange Polska on April 16, 2012, and Frances Orange S.A. currently holds just over half its shares. Orange Polska itself refers to the site internally as Centrum Technologiczne Orange Polska, its Orange Polska Technology Center, with Warsaw Data Hub serving as the facilitys external marketing name, and third party directory listings confirm the four 400 square meter data halls and October 2021 completion independently of Oranges own press materials, while continuing to withhold specific power capacity and total floor area figures from public disclosure.
